_doc: The 1904 context city: faded stand-ins for every part of the map not yet built (T-2477), its streets and its reach to the haze (T-2491). GENERATED by tools/build_context_1904.py -- do not hand-edit; re-run the tool. Local ENU metres of data/datum.json. Drawn by renderers/web/js/context.js, which fades them and drops any a placed structure touches.

tiers.sheet_outline: inferred -- the smallest rectangle holding each part a Sanborn 1911 sheet draws, carried to 1904 on Glessner House's reading that these sheets changed only at 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie (Prairie lots are not read here); north of 16th Street, what Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws, carried eighteen years forward
tiers.sheet_material: inferred -- the map's own colour: pink brick, blue stone, yellow frame
tiers.projection: reconstructed -- no map of this ground is in hand: streets on the grid the section corners and the street grid measure, lots on the measured frontages, buildings by the zone the 1904 city's known uses give the block
tiers.streets: measured where a crossing is read (the street grid's own, the section corners), filled at the pitch those readings give elsewhere; the carriageway's 38 ft is the grid's row_66
tiers.height_roof_colour_trees: reconstructed -- by `rules`; the maps' storey figures are not read

dwelling_masonry.why: a brick or stone house of 2-3 storeys on a raised basement, the '3B' and '2B' the sheets print most often on these faces

wing.why: a drawn range behind or beside the main body: the sheets' rear '2B'

porch.why: a part under 25 m2 and under a quarter of the main body

outbuilding.why: a separate rear building under 110 m2: the sheets' 2-storey stables, barns and sheds (a 1911 garage read as a stable)

block.why: a building over 450 m2: flats, an institution or a works, 3-4 storeys under a flat roof

roof.why: a house is gabled along its long side or flat behind a cornice, about half each for masonry and always gabled for frame; a rise of 0.35-0.5 of the span

house_row.why: past the near ring a run of three to six houses is drawn as one row, at the house rules' heights: at that distance the haze leaves a third or less of its colour and a row reads as the houses would; on a sheet, a drawn building at least 3.5 times as long as it is deep and no deeper than 16 m is a row of attached houses, not a block (T-2833: Mortimer and Tappan's sixteen lots on 16th Street, Robinson plate 10), at the house rules' heights under a flat roof

shops_block.why: State Street and Wabash Avenue south of Twelfth: brick business blocks of three and four storeys, shops under flats, to the lot line

business_block.why: Twelfth Street to Harrison: the wholesale and printing district's lofts, five to seven storeys

loop_block.why: north of Harrison: the downtown's office and loft blocks, eight to sixteen storeys

railway_shed.why: the railway lands: freight houses and engine sheds, long and low

readings.what: 1st Presbyterian Church, Indiana Avenue at 21st Street
readings.printed: '48' to eaves'; a hip roof drawn in dashes

readings.what: Thompson-Reid & Collins Bros. Ice Cream Co., Indiana at 16th

palette._why: Colour families, not colours: the sheets give the material, and each building takes one tone of its family by a seeded draw. Chicago's own brick ran red to the cream 'Milwaukee' brick; its stone fronts were Joliet-Lemont limestone and brownstone.

projection.frontages_from: 83 Indiana and Calumet lots of data/street_grid/1904.json

zones.residential: houses on lots, as the traced sheets' own faces: the default
zones.workers: west of Canal Street: the frame cottages and flats of the Near West Side and Bridgeport, seven in ten frame
zones.shops: State Street and Wabash Avenue from Twelfth to 22nd: three- and four-storey brick business blocks
zones.business: Twelfth Street to Harrison, east of Canal Street: the near-south wholesale and printing district, five to seven storeys
zones.loop: north of Harrison, east of Canal Street: the downtown's office and loft blocks, eight to sixteen storeys
zones.railway: Clark Street to Canal Street from Twelfth to 22nd: the railway lands and the river (the terminal yards of the stations at Polk Street and Twelfth, and the South Branch through them): long sheds, no houses

clearance._doc:
THE SWEEP (T-3038; the owner, 2026-10-22: "you put a building in the middle of the street,
fix this and any others"). Every stand-in is tested as its whole rectangle, not its centre,
against the ground keep_off() names and against the stand-ins already kept. A sheet's drawn
part is cut back off a roadway, an alley or the railway (its smallest rectangle overran the
line the sheet draws) and its parts may overlap each other, as one drawn building's do; a
projected stand-in is cut back off all of that and off every kept stand-in, or dropped. Trees
keep off roadways, alleys, the right of way, the faded streets and every kept stand-in.

network._doc:
The streets of the city the context draws, as lines of constant u (the avenues, which
run north and south) and of constant v (the cross streets). Each line says what places it.

MEASURED where the project holds a reading: Michigan, Indiana, Prairie and Calumet, and
16th to 22nd, as data/street_grid/1904.json and the terrain spec place them; State and
Halsted, Madison and Twelfth (Roosevelt) at the school section's corners, read from
OpenStreetMap for T-0878 (data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_nara_hup_section_corners.json, and
G1 of wright_1834_nara_hup_gcps.json for State and Madison). Chicago's section lines run
down the middle of the streets laid on them.
FILLED between and past those at the pitch they give (RECONSTRUCTED, LIBERTY_STREETS): the
section's mile cut in sixteen across (the city's lots face the avenues, two 125 ft lots and
an alley to a block) and in eight along (its cross streets an eighth of a mile apart); three
numbered streets between Twelfth and 16th (the four intervals measure 203 m each); Twenty-
second to Thirty-first a mile, as the section lines run, in nine; Wabash midway between
State and Michigan; and Calumet's pitch repeated east until the water.
